mike: quick thread — different take on the demote+evict stale-read we saw. I want to propose a watermark+replay handshake instead of an explicit fence. tara: curious. how's watermark+replay different from the fence ideas we already discussed? mike: short version: instead of an additional control-plane 'fence' write, the old owner publishes a durable prefix-watermark W = max_seq_applied (cheap, tiny) and exposes a short ephemeral delta-log (replay segment) that new owners can pull during takeover. new owner either sees W>=expected_seq or replays deltas from old owner to catch up. sasha: so owner keeps an append-only mini-log for in-memory deltas that is flushed to local staging synchronously on demote. new owner either trusts watermark or pulls the replay segment. How do we guarantee the replay is alive after crash? mike: good question. we have a few tiers: - tier0 (strict): watermark is persisted to control-plane plus replay segment is wrote to staging and replicated to a small number of local peers (via our sidecar). new owner will fetch from staging/peers. - tier1 (balanced): watermark persisted to control-plane, replay kept on owner disk only (fast), if owner crashed new owner falls back to stall+read-repair. - tier2 (fast): watermark only in-memory exposed via short-lifetime beacon; best-effort replay via RPC; fast but not crash-safe. lee: that's interesting. advantage: watermark is a very small metadata write with a clear monotonic meaning. replay segment provides the actual deltas to reconcile without forcing full WAL. Also lets us tune durability per tenant. tara: how do we compute expected_seq? from handoff-token? we need a coordinate so new owner knows which seq it requires. mike: plan: demote produces a handoff object H = {epoch_next, required_seq}. required_seq is the highest admitted sequence (including inflight writes assigned a seq). old owner atomically publishes watermark W >= admitted_seq after writing replay segment. new owner on seeing H: - if W >= required_seq -> safe to serve - else -> attempt pull replay from owner (RPC to owner-staging or peer replicas) - if pull fails and owner unreachable -> stall or trigger repair based on tenant policy sasha: where do we store replay segment? short-lived file in /var/lib/redwood/prefix-replay/--. we can let garbage collector remove after N minutes once commit confirmed. minimal metadata required: digest, min_seq, max_seq, size. lee: telemetry: demote_watermark_publish_lat, replay_pull_count, replay_pull_latency, demote_stall_count_on_missing_replay. Also include a per-handoff trace id. tara: how about eviction interplay? if replay segment is only on-disk, eviction that frees RAM is fine; we just need replay available on disk. But if eviction also deletes staging files (we currently delete staging aggressively), we must change eviction to preserve replay files until demote complete. mike: exactly — eviction policy tweak: when demote in progress, promote replay files to protected staging (short TTL) and avoid deleting them. That avoids heavy soft-pinning of RAM and instead pins a small disk footprint. sasha: nice. that reduces memory churn relative to soft-pins and keeps a durable reconciliation path. but we must ensure disk I/O doesn't become a bottleneck under high demote churn. add a canary to throttle demote concurrency or spill replays to remote object store if local IO saturates. lee: crash scenarios: if owner crashes before watermark persisted but after reply acked demote completion, new owner must assume worst-case (inflight lost). So demote must make watermark persist before acknowledging demote success to cluster. That implies an extra step but watermark write is tiny so cost is low. mike: agreed. demote commit order: (1) create replay segment atomically from in-memory deltas, flush to disk (or replicate), (2) persist watermark to control-plane, (3) acknowledge demote. If crash between 1 and 2, new owner will see no watermark and will stall and call recovery. tara: any client-visible latency hit? small, because disk flush of a tiny replay segment is faster than full WAL and we avoid holding large in-memory pins. For strict mode we replicate replay to a peer which adds network IO but still bounded. sasha: we should add read-path optimization: if new owner serves a read and sees epoch bump but watermark < required_seq, it can opportunistically pull replay and apply just-in-time for that read instead of stalling completely. That reduces full-stall occurrences. mike: yes, optimistic-apply: read-handler detects mismatch, issues background replay pull+apply, waits up to short timeout T_read_fast; if still not ready, fall back to stall or read-repair depending on tenant. We must ensure idempotency and ordering when applying replays. lee: operational knobs: default = tier0 for enterprise (replicate replay, persist watermark), tier1 for standard, tier2 fast for dev. Expose flags: redwood.kv.handoff.mode = {strict,balanced,fast} and redwood.kv.handoff.replay_ttl_seconds. tara: tests: add chaos job "replay-protect-demote" that exercises demote+evict+owner-crash, validate no stale reads for tier0 and tier1 (with stall+repair), and assert reduced memory churn vs soft-pin baseline. sasha: add runbook entries: where to look for replay files, how to force replay rehydrate, and how to clear stuck demotes. include commands: ``` # inspect replay files for prefix ls -lh /var/lib/redwood/prefix-replay/-* # force push replay to peer redwoodctl replay push --prefix=

--to-peer= ``` mike: action items: - mike: prototype replay-segment writer + watermark publish + disk-protect flow (ETA: 1w) - sasha: spec handoff object shape and control-plane API for watermark (ETA: 3d) - lee: add telemetry + canary config + dashboard panels (ETA: 4d) - tara: add chaos test and runbook snippets (ETA: 3d) canary-bot: created ticket IR-20001: "watermark-replay-handoff-protocol" and scheduled canary job CR-77. mike: ok will open PR with prototype and perf notes. leaning this approach because it buys crash-safety without heavy RAM pinning. objections? sasha: none from me. seems like a good middle ground and different enough from fence-only approaches. tara: agree. prefer disk-protected replay vs soft-pin for memory-sensitive tenants. lee: fine. prioritize tests. mike: closing thread, will post PR link when ready.
